title: Instrumentation sidecar adapter and zero-copy span path
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Replace ad-hoc OTEL instrumentation per-service with a lightweight sidecar adapter that centralizes trace/span enrichment, sampling decisions, and proto-friendly span forwarding. The adapter will expose a zero-copy fast path for hot request flows (service -> sidecar -> telemetry collector) to reduce allocation pressure in the runtime process. Goals: 1) reduce p50/p99 CPU for runtime processes by 10-25% for typical inference traffic, 2) lower telemetry-induced allocation and GC churn, 3) enable uniform sampling and attribute normalization without touching app code, 4) simplify multi-language instrumentation strategy.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end trace flow implemented via sidecar adapter for Java and Go runtimes
Hotpath zero-copy path demonstrated in benchmark with at least 12% CPU reduction at p99 in synthetic load
No increase in end-to-end request p99 latency > 3ms after introducing sidecar (measured under normal load)
Instrumentation compatibility shim for existing span attributes so dashboards and trace IDs remain stable
Automated canary rollout plan and rollback playbook documented in the runbook
tasks: Design: sketch sidecar API and wire protocol (binary envelope) - Aisha
PoC: Go zero-copy span serializer and minimal sidecar - Marco
Instrument: add sidecar client to runtime lib with feature flag - Priya
Bench: microbench and end-to-end load tests comparing current vs sidecar flows - Bench team
Rollout: staged canary to 5% -> 25% -> 100% with metrics gates
Docs: add architecture diagram and troubleshooting steps to Confluence
comments: 2025-11-03 - Aisha Patel: Initial discovery — engines observe non-trivial allocations from OTEL spans during KV cache hits. Talked with Runtime team; sidecar appeared promising to offload common enrichment work.

2025-11-05 - Marco Chen: PoC complete. Zero-copy span encoder in Go reduced per-request allocations by ~40% in microbench (single-threaded). PoC repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/otel-sidecar-poc (internal).

2025-11-08 - Priya Nair: Integration note — added feature flag runtime.telemetry.sidecar_enabled. Default remains false until canary. Need a minimal compatibility layer to keep attribute keys stable across old traces.

2025-11-11 - Bench Team: End-to-end load test (1000 qps, mixed seq lengths) shows runtime CPU down 14% at p95 and 19% at p99; sidecar process adds ~2.5% infra CPU. Detailed results: https://drive.redwood/bench/sidecar-2025-11-11.xlsx

2025-11-12 - Security (Danielle): Reviewed network/privileges. Sidecar communicates over loopback; require egress policy doc for Private deployments. No KMS exposure. Marked security_review_required = false for now, will revisit for on-prem package.

2025-11-15 - Marco Chen: Trade-offs discussion — sidecar reduces allocations but introduces an extra hop. We added batching in the sidecar for low-volume requests to amortize overhead; small latency regression is within ACs.

2025-11-18 - Aisha Patel: Design decision — adopt compact binary envelope for spans to avoid JSON allocations. Will map current span attributes to stable schema via normalization table in the sidecar; change log added to design doc.
2025-11-19 - Marco Chen: PR opened for runtime shim and PoC sidecar: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1248 (internal). Requesting review from @runtime-team and @observability.
2025-11-21 - Priya Nair: Canary plan drafted in runbook. Gate checks: error rate, p99 latency, telemetry ingestion rate, CPU. Will start 5% canary on 2025-11-24 pending approvals.
